findings: The plan now gives the exact Higham–Mao–Stuart strong-rate assumptions and conclusion: C1 coefficients, one-sided Lipschitz drift, globally Lipschitz diffusion, polynomial local-Lipschitz drift, and uniform finite moments of all orders for the exact solution and both Euler interpolations imply mean-square uniform error O(h).
The theorem’s proof uses localization/moment truncation, interpolation defect estimates, Ito formula, BDG, and Gronwall; no unjustified all-purpose L2 assumption is left.

Särkkä–Solin §8.3 defines weak error and gives the Euler weak-order statement under sufficient regularity, but does not prove it. The scaffold therefore uses a local backward-Kolmogorov proof design with a stated C^(2,4) polynomial-growth solution class and moment premises, plus a separate obligation deriving that class from coefficient/test assumptions.

The coupled-level MLMC correction claim is conditional on shared Brownian increments and a globally Lipschitz payoff; the O(h) variance follows from the strong O(h) mean-square fine/coarse coupling, and per-sample work O(h^-1) is explicit.

The weak-rate design now states a checkable conservative moment condition: if the backward solution derivatives grow at most C(1+||x||^q), assume uniform exact/Euler moments of order p≥2q+8 on fixed [0,T], obtainable from finite pth initial moment under global Lipschitz/linear-growth coefficients; no undefined “enough moments” remains.
